THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Both the appeals arise out of judgment and award dated 04th February, 2022 passed in MVC No.5 of 2017 by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kushtagi (for brevity,
hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").
NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB 2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to as per their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, on 27th February, 2016 the petitioner went on his motorcycle bearing No.KA- 08/K-5192 for his personal work and while returning back, at about 8.30 pm when he was proceeding on Navalgund-Ron Road and was driving the motorcycle slowly on his left side near Mallapur, the respondent No.1 entered the drove the lorry bearing Registration No.KA-26/3465 without showing indicators or any signal and the petitioner lost control and dashed to the lorry at it back, as a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his backbone and head Ashok S/O Basappa Harlapur Since ... vs Lingappa Alias Ningappa S/O ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87286811/
4 and right hand and all over the body and became unconscious.
The injured was shifted to Government Hospital at Ron where he was given first aid treatment and then was referred to higher hospital and hence taken to German Hospital.

There the petitioner was referred to KLE Hospital,
Belagavi wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and operated to spinal cord and even after treatment for more than two and a half months, petitioner did not recover and further after discharge from KLE Hospital, Belagavi, the NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB petitioner was again admitted to Balaji Neuron Science Hospital, Hubballi wherein he was treated for two to three months, but he could not recover and became permanently disabled.

It is contended that prior to accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was aged 37 years and was doing Government job and also agriculture work and getting an income of Rs.29,713/- per month.

It is further contended that respondent No.1 who is the driver and respondent No.2 who is the owner and respondent No.3 the insurer, are jointly and severally responsible to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, preferred the claim petition.
4. In response to Notice, respondent No.1 was placed ex-parte and respondents 2 and 3 appeared through their counsel.
Respondent No.2 has not filed any written statement.
Respondent No.3 filed written statement denying the accident and denying the petition averments.
It is further contended that the owner has violated the policy conditions and the driver of the lorry was not having valid licence and hence prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed issues for its consideration.
To prove the case of petitioner, two witnesses were examined as PWs1 and 2 and NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB 34 documents were marked as ExhibitsP1 to P34.
On behalf of respondents one witness was examined as RW1 and eight documents were marked as Exhibits R1 to R8.

Upon hearing both the parties, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.88,57,228/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation and the insurance was directed to deposit 80% of compensation amount along with interest holding that the rider of the motorcycle has contributed to the accident to the extent of 20%.

Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the National Insurance Company Limited has preferred Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101291 of 2022, questioning the liability and also the quantum of compensation.
The claimants have preferred Miscellaneous First Appeal No.102187 of 2022 seeking enhancement of compensation.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant- Insurance Company submits that the apportionment of negligence on the part of the lorry to the extent of 80% is erroneous and against the oral and documentary evidence on records.

He submits that immediately after the accident, the person who has given complaint before the police has clearly NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB stated that due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle by the petitioner himself, when there is clear oral and documentary evidence on record to show that the petitioner himself is negligent for occurrence of accident for which the police have filed charge sheet against the petitioner.
The Tribunal without looking into the material evidence apportioned 80% negligence upon the Insurance, is arbitrary and without due application of mind.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering 100% disability to the whole body and added 40% as future prospects towards the income of the petitioner.
It is submitted that the petitioner is a government employee and is the beneficiary of medical expenses and entitled for future benefits for not able to do any work.

The Tribunal without discussing this aspect of the matter has considered the disability at Ashok S/O Basappa Harlapur Since ... vs Lingappa Alias Ningappa S/O ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87286811/
5 100% and added 40% future prospects which is not permissible under law and when the injured person is government employee, he is not entitled under the head loss of future income until and unless he has not received any benefit from the department he is serving.

The act of the Tribunal while considering the disability is arbitrary and without due application of mind and against the NC:
2023:KHC-D:11058-DB documentary evidence on record.
Hence he submits that the impugned judgment and award is liable to be interfered with.
6. As against this, the learned counsel for the claimants submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is very meager and same is not in accordance with law.

The Tribunal has not appreciated the materials placed on record which were sufficient to hold that claimant was not negligent and temporary injunction was the only the driver of the offending lorry who entered the road without any indicators was the cause for accident.

Hence, the ought not to have attributed 20%
negligence on the claimant which requires to be set aside.
The Tribunal has not awarded attended charges for the rest of life.

The Tribunal has not considered the grievousness of injuries and hence,
the award of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering is too low and hence prays for enhancement.

The Tribunal has failed to note that claimant was forced to take voluntary retirement with effect from 30thNovember, 2019; and hence, ought to have taken income of the claimant at Rs.42,000/-
per month.
Hence, he prays that enhancement is required under this head also.
On all - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB these grounds he prays for enhancement of compensation, by allowing the appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the following points would arise for our consideration in these appeals:
1.
Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as regards quantum of compensation?
2. Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
3. What order or award?

8. Our answer for the above points are as under:
Point No.1: in the negative Point No.2: in the negative Point No.3: as per final order Regarding Point No.1:
9.
We have carefully examined the material on record.

Accident is not in dispute and the petitioner suffering injuries in - 11 - Ashok S/O Basappa Harlapur Since ... vs Lingappa Alias Ningappa S/O ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87286811/
6 NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB
the said accident is also not in dispute.

The police have submitted charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry for commission of offences under Section 279,
338 and 304A of Indian Penal Code.

RW1-Honnali Anand, who is working as Assistant in National Insurance Company limited, has deposed in his evidence that on 27th February, 2016 at about 8.30 pm the petitioner rode the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and dashed against the vehicle of respondent No.2 from the back side.
Further, the petitioner's vehicle was not insured.
One Shebber has given complaint against the petitioner as regards to his rash and negligent act.
After investigation, Ron police have filed charge sheet against the petitioner for offence punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of Indian Penal Code.
R2 has violated the policy conditions.
the respondent No.1 was not holding valid driving licence as on the date of alleged accident.

As per driving licence extract issued by RTO, the same reveals that the respondent No.1 got renewed his driving licence for transport vehicle and the same was valid from 28th June 2016 to 27th June, 2019.
The alleged accident occurred on 27th February, 2016.
Hence, for violation of policy conditions, the Insurer is - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB not liable to pay compensation.

During the course of cross- examination, he has clearly admitted that the respondent No.1 has pleaded guilty before the court of JMFC for the alleged commission of offence under Section 283 of Indian Penal Code.
On careful examination of evidence on record, it is crystal clear that the driver of the offending lorry, has not followed Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules.
RW1 has not whispered anything as to why the driver of the offending lorry has abruptly stopped the vehicle on highway.
Had the driver of the lorry followed the abovesaid rules and regulations, the accident would not have occurred.

Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly held that there is negligence on the part of the deceased to the accident in question to the extent of 20% and the driver of the lorry had contributed 80%to the accident.

On re-appreciation of evidence on record, we do not find any illegality/legal infirmity in the observation made by the Tribunal as to the negligent act on the part of the lorry driver and also on the rider of motorcycle.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in the negative.

OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, PRAYING TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AWARDED BY THE TRIBUNAL FROM 88,57,228=00 TO 1,00,000=00 BY FIXING 100% LIABILITY ON THE VEHICLE BELONGING TO THE RESPONDENT NO.2 BY MODIFYING THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 04.02.2022 PASSED IN MVC NO.5/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, AT KUSHTAGI, AND AWARDING JUST COMPENSATION AS DEEMED FIT AND PROPER ALONG WITH INTEREST.
THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
opennyai_summary.facts:
Upon hearing both the parties, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.88,57,228/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation and the insurance was directed to deposit 80% of compensation amount along with interest holding that the rider of the motorcycle has contributed to the accident to the extent of 20%.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the National Insurance Company Limited has preferred Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101291 of 2022, questioning the liability and also the quantum of compensation.
The claimants have preferred Miscellaneous First Appeal No.102187 of 2022 seeking enhancement of compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The act of the Tribunal while considering the disability is arbitrary and without due application of mind and against the NC:
2023:KHC-D:11058-DB documentary evidence on record.
The Tribunal has not appreciated the materials placed on record which were sufficient to hold that claimant was not negligent and temporary injunction was the only the driver of the offending lorry who entered the road without any indicators was the cause for accident.
Hence, the ought not to have attributed 20%
negligence on the claimant which requires to be set aside.
The Tribunal has not awarded attended charges for the rest of life.
The Tribunal has not considered the grievousness of injuries and hence,
the award of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering is too low and hence prays for enhancement.
The Tribunal has failed to note that claimant was forced to take voluntary retirement with effect from 30thNovember, 2019; and hence, ought to have taken income of the claimant at Rs.42,000/-
per month.
opennyai_summary.issue:
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the following points would arise for our consideration in these appeals:
1.
Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as regards quantum of compensation?
2. Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
R2 has violated the policy conditions.
the respondent No.1 was not holding valid driving licence as on the date of alleged accident.
The alleged accident occurred on 27th February, 2016.
Hence, for violation of policy conditions, the Insurer is - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11058-DB not liable to pay compensation.
During the course of cross- examination, he has clearly admitted that the respondent No.1 has pleaded guilty before the court of JMFC for the alleged commission of offence under Section 283 of Indian Penal Code.
On careful examination of evidence on record, it is crystal clear that the driver of the offending lorry, has not followed Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules.
RW1 has not whispered anything as to why the driver of the offending lorry has abruptly stopped the vehicle on highway.
Had the driver of the lorry followed the abovesaid rules and regulations, the accident would not have occurred.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly held that there is negligence on the part of the deceased to the accident in question to the extent of 20% and the driver of the lorry had contributed 80%to the accident.
The insured died after the judgment passed by the Tribunal.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, we answer point No.2 in the negative.
For the foregoing reasons and discussions, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1. Appeals are dismissed;
2. Amount in deposit if any, be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
